Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a general orientation (both in English and Japanese) for 2 hours, and the NUPACE office will deliver you all the information by email. They have an information storage system, and you can find everything related in it. (The exchange is online)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The general questions regarding courses register and the necessary documentation.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy, the system is very simple to use.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1. Some of the professors can not speak English (especially for the Japanese language courses), if you can not speak Japanese, please choose the G30 courses. 
2. In Japan, if you want to take a course, you should send an email and ask those professors to add you manually. This may take a very long time, be aware of the registration deadline. :)
3. Ask NUPACE office if you have any kinds of questions! They will reply you very soon!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
NP courses: you will have an exam before the semester if you want to take the language course. So you will be sent to the most suitable course :)
General courses: Equivalent to the master courses in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
1. Attendance is important, be aware of the quizzes during class.
2. Daily homework is common, maybe 300-600 words per lecture.
3. Students are shyer in Japan, so the discussion section maybe always silent.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
NP2 Japanese
Climate change and Infrastructure
Culture & Psychology
Japan's development experience
GIS: Agritourism in Japan
Sustainability and environmental studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Please do the GIS (Guided independent study) at Nagoya University! I highly recommend trying it under the supervision of a Japanese professor. It is very interesting and you will learn more than the knowledge from this experience. Although I can not do some onsite research, I really find a lot of exciting information about agritourism in Japan. Moreover, my professor invited me to his lab seminar and I learned a lot from the following students. 
And the Japanese course! Those teachers are sweet and supportive, they can help you to have a better experience in Japan :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Please be aware that many Japanese people can not speak English.
2. Some lectures will be very early (before 9 AM), which means you may need to get up very early.
3. Enjoy the culture and make friends!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to learn more from the NP courses, please learn Japanese in advance.

questions.answer: The 20 pages of the research report, is great preparation for my master thesis.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Wake up at 7:30 and start the zoom Japanese lecture.
